info.label: What {name} is
copy.label: Copy id {id}
info.s:level_overworld: One tick of the Overworld. The first level of a tick also reads the network and runs the parts of the tick that every level shares, so on most servers this is the whole tick and every phase below sits inside it.
info.s:level_the_nether: One tick of the Nether: every phase below runs for the Nether's blocks, mobs and players.
info.s:level_the_end: One tick of the End: every phase below runs for the End's blocks, mobs and players.
info.s:tick_blocks: The block phase of a tick: chunk tickets, scheduled block and fluid ticks, random ticks, block events and moving pistons. It grows with redstone, flowing water and lava, growing plants and the number of loaded chunks.
info.s:tb_tickets: Chunk tickets that time out, and the work of choosing which chunks tick this tick.
info.s:tb_chunks: Picks the loaded chunks that get random ticks this tick, from the players' simulation distance.
info.s:tb_entity_inside: Blocks that react to something standing in them: pressure plates, tripwires, detector rails and buttons under players, minecarts, arrows and mobs.
info.s:tb_scheduled: Scheduled block ticks that are due: everything a block asked to run later, such as redstone repeaters and comparators, falling sand and gravel, and leaves checking their distance to a log. Each tick's side effects apply before the next one runs.
info.s:tb_fluids: Scheduled fluid ticks that are due: water and lava spreading and flowing.
info.s:random_ticks: Random ticks: every loaded ticking chunk picks random blocks each tick, so crops grow, leaves decay and grass spreads. The cost grows with loaded chunks and with the random tick speed game rule.
info.s:tb_broadcast: Sends this tick's block changes to the players who can see them.
info.s:tb_block_events: Block events: pistons extending, note blocks playing, chests opening and the like.
info.s:tb_level_events: The sounds, particles and other effects that the block phase asked for.
info.s:tb_pistons: Moving pistons: copies the blocks being pushed into the world so collisions and drawing can see them.
info.s:tick_mobs: The mob phase: natural spawning and every mob's thinking and movement, plus the per-tick upkeep of statistics, scoreboards, boss bars, the world border and advancements.
info.s:spawn_natural: Natural mob spawning: counts the loaded mobs per category, then tries to spawn new ones in each player's spawning chunks. The cost grows with the number of players and mobs.
info.s:sn_candidates: Finds the chunks around each player where mobs may spawn this tick.
info.s:sn_inhabited: Adds to each candidate chunk's inhabited time, which raises the local difficulty there.
info.s:sn_level: Sets up the view of the level that spawning reads from.
info.s:sn_materialize: Lists the loaded mobs and the players that the spawn counts are built from.
info.s:sn_state: Builds the spawn state: how many mobs of each category the level and each chunk hold.
info.s:sn_categories: Chooses which mob categories may spawn this tick, under their caps.
info.s:sn_shuffle: Shuffles the candidate chunks with the level's random numbers, in vanilla's order.
info.s:sn_attempts: The spawn attempts themselves: for each chunk and category, picks positions and checks whether a mob fits. Usually the heaviest part of spawning.
info.s:sn_finalize: Creates the mobs the attempts chose and adds them to the level.
info.s:tick_creature_entities: Thinking and moving for every loaded mob: pathfinding, goals, senses and attacks. The cost grows with the number of mobs and with how much each one is doing.
info.s:creature_prepare: Prepares the mobs' tick: lists the mobs, villagers and solid mobs, and the block changes that affect paths.
info.s:creature_loop: Runs each mob's own tick in turn: its goals, movement and attacks.
info.s:tick_lan: Everything the server does for connected players in a tick: it applies their actions, then sends each player the level's chunks, block changes and nearby entities. Single player runs it too, through its own server.
info.s:tick_lan_packets: Reads and applies the packets players sent since the last tick, such as digging, placing and movement, before the block phase runs.
info.s:lan_drain: Takes the packets that are waiting from every player.
info.s:lan_events: Carries out the actions the players' packets asked for.
info.s:lan_guests: Runs each connected player's own tick: mining, item use and pickups, before the tick is described to their clients.
info.s:lan_entity_states: Works out where every entity is and how it looks, ready to send to players.
info.s:lan_tick_level: Brings the connected players' view of a level up to date: chunks, block changes, containers, nearby entities and their own state.
info.s:lan_chunks: Sends world chunks to players. It picks each player's next batch by distance, encodes each column once however many players need it, and sends them. It is heavy when players join or move fast and need many chunks at once.
info.s:lan_block_changes: Sends this tick's light and block changes to the players who can see them.
info.s:lan_containers: Sends changes in open containers to the players looking at them.
info.s:lan_track_entities: Decides which entities each player can see, and sends spawns, movements and removals.
info.s:lan_player_state: Sends each player's own state: health, hunger and status effects.
info.s:lan_end_tick: Player list upkeep after every level has ticked, such as the latency updates.
info.s:streaming: Chunk streaming: collects the chunks that worker threads finished (generating, lighting, meshing), schedules more around the players and unloads far ones. It spikes when players move into new terrain.
info.s:lt_block: Recalculates block light (torches, lava, glowstone) around the positions that changed.
info.s:lt_columns: Finds the lowest sky-lit block of each changed column, which decides where sky light has to be recalculated.
info.s:lt_sky: Recalculates sky light around the positions that changed.
info.s:postprocess_chunks: Finishes freshly generated chunks once their neighbours have loaded: water and lava next to open air, block shape fixes and bubble columns. This is what starts cave waterfalls and lava falls.
info.s:tick_items: Ticks every dropped item: its movement, merging with nearby items and pickup.
info.s:tick_block_entities: Ticks the blocks that hold data, such as chests, furnaces, hoppers and brewing stands.
info.s:tick_hud: Per-tick upkeep of titles, the saving indicator and the held item's name.
info.s:entity_portals: Looks for items, mobs, boats, minecarts and arrows that touched a portal and moves them through it.
info.s:tick_sculk_entities: The entity side of sculk: the warden spawn tracker and the vibrations from entities walking over blocks.
info.s:tick_moving_pistons: Moves the pistons that are in the middle of pushing, and the entities they carry.
info.s:tick_effects: Ticks the status effects of players and the potions in flight.
info.s:tick_particles: Advances every live particle by one tick.
info.s:prepare: Everything the game does on its own thread to get a frame ready, before the graphics card is asked to draw: culling, entity and HUD geometry, weather.
info.s:renderer: Hands the prepared frame to the renderer, which uploads data, builds the draw lists and records every render pass.
info.s:occlusion: Starts the cave culling search on its worker thread, which decides which chunk sections are hidden behind terrain.
info.s:visibility: Walks the loaded chunk sections and keeps the ones the camera can see.
info.s:gpu culling: Prepares the graphics card's own culling of near chunk sections.
info.s:hud: Builds the heads-up display for the frame: hotbar, hearts, chat and every overlay.
info.s:entity_geometry: Builds the geometry of every visible entity for the frame.
info.s:weather: Builds the rain and snow geometry around the camera.
info.s:encode: Finishes the recorded command buffer so it can be sent to the graphics card.
info.s:submit: Hands the finished frame to the graphics card's queue.
info.s:clouds: Prepares the cloud mesh for the frame.
info.f:kq3h1qx3: Reads one block state from a chunk section's compressed storage. It is cheap on its own, so a high count means something is scanning many blocks, such as random ticks, light or fluid updates.
info.f:kd5efx0c: Looks up the block at a position: finds the chunk, then the entry inside it. Every check of a neighbouring block goes through here.
info.f:v6z0x118: Takes the next due scheduled tick off a chunk's queue. Lots of time here means lots of scheduled block or fluid ticks.
info.f:masspbf6: Runs the block update queue: after a block changes, its neighbours are told in vanilla's order, which can cascade through redstone and falling blocks.
info.f:j0r8pnm6: Tells each neighbour of a changed block so it can reshape itself: fences connect, stairs turn, redstone wire links up.
info.f:prmwv9hs: Finds the next chunk section that holds blocks a random tick can act on, so empty sections are skipped.
info.f:rxy0knt1: Runs one due scheduled tick for a block or a fluid.
info.f:kgj3xre6: The chunk streaming step of a tick. It is the function behind the streaming phase.
info.f:21zxev5z: The connected-player work of one level: chunks, block changes, tracked entities and player state.
info.f:s37sytrt: Sends the tick's block changes to the players who can see them.
info.f:73bj7bmj: Encodes a chunk section into the form players receive it in.
info.f:nqc8sf3d: Encodes chunk columns ahead of sending them, on helper threads.
info.f:y7z04p5v: One server tick from the top: every phase of every level runs under it.
info.f:apf3y50m: The memory allocator preparing a fresh page for small allocations. It shows up when a phase allocates a lot, such as building many short-lived lists.
info.f:d1dtaa7r: Copies a block of memory: moving chunk data, building packets, growing lists. A high own time means large copies.
info.f:7dnvdqkz: Time the profiler could not tie to a function: code in system libraries or graphics drivers that carry no symbols.
info.f:rhk2pnfw: Asks the operating system to release or reuse memory. The allocator calls it when it gives memory back.
info.f:yr5ja1xt: A direct call into the operating system. The function that called it shows what was asked for.
info.f:rr803w1x: Prepares and submits one frame to the graphics card: it tidies the mesh buffers, then runs every render pass.
info.f:2z9g69ht: The thread is waiting in the operating system for its next event or timer. That is idle time, not work.
info.f:wbme93ry: Picks which faces of a chunk section's mesh point toward the camera, so back faces are not drawn.
info.f:m8r50yj8: Changes one block and runs what follows: updates to its neighbours and their shapes, each of which can change more blocks. Redstone and flowing liquids spend much of their time here.
info.f:hq3s03eb: Sets up the view of the level that block behaviour runs against (weather, sky darkness, the player's box and collision) and runs the code inside it. Its own time is that set-up.
info.f:nvyr76w7: Collects this tick's due scheduled ticks from the loaded chunks, up to the per-tick maximum, in vanilla's order.
info.f:z87ymr7d: Runs a block's scheduled tick by picking the behaviour of its kind, such as crops, falling blocks, leaves or redstone parts.
info.f:whfctzya: A wrapper that marks which dimension block behaviour runs in. It has almost no time of its own: everything inside it counts toward its total.
